title: Admonitory Sayings on Buddha-Recitation (Four Passages)
excerpt: Those who practice the Pure Land must plainly oppose birth and death — this is not a matter to merely speak of and then let rest. You must reflect that impermanence is swift and time waits for no one, and make this one single task of your life. If you advance halfway and retreat halfway, half believing and half doubting, then when it comes (when it comes to the moment of death), what use will it be? How can you escape the cycle of rebirth?

inline.s: Excerpted from Xifang Gongju (Evidence of the Western Land)
When the skandha of perception stirs, Māra gains his opportunity;
Buddha-recitation, the wondrous medicine, cures precisely this ailment.

Those who practice the Pure Land must plainly oppose birth and death — this is not a matter to merely speak of and then let rest. You must reflect that impermanence is swift and time waits for no one, and make this one single task of your life. If you advance halfway and retreat halfway, half believing and half doubting, then when it comes
when it comes to the moment of death
what use will it be
How can you escape the cycle of rebirth
If your faith is sufficient, then from today onward rouse great courage and great diligence. Do not ask whether you understand
"Do you understand?" is a Chan term meaning: have you awakened?

, or whether you see your true nature. Simply hold fast to the one phrase "Namo Amitabha Buddha," leaning on it as on Mount Sumeru, so that it cannot be shaken or moved. Concentrate your mind, unify your intention, whether by reciting while investigating
contemplating
recollecting
reciting ten times, or by silent recitation
focused recitation
binding recitation
bowing recitation — keep the mind on it and never let it go
never forgetting it for a single thought

, ever recollecting and ever reciting. Recite in the morning, recite in the evening, recite while walking, recite while sitting. Let no thought pass in vain; let the recitation never leave the mind. Day by day, hour by hour, do not let it go. Dense and unbroken, like a hen sitting on her eggs, ever keeping the warmth continuous — this is pure mindfulness in unbroken succession.
If you add to this the illumination of wisdom
the contemplation of wisdom
, you will know that the Pure Land is none other than your own mind. This is the practice of one of superior wisdom.

If you can thus hold firm, be your own master, and lean steadily, then even when states of pain and pleasure, adversity and ease, appear before you, simply recite Amitabha Buddha. Let there be no thought that wavers, no thought that retreats or slackens, no thought of scattered fancy, until the end of your life, with never any other thought, determined to be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss in the West.
If you can truly practice in this way, then the karmic obstructions of ignorance and birth and death accumulated over kalpas will naturally melt away

the defilements and habitual outflows will naturally be purified without remainder. You will personally see Amitabha without ever leaving this very thought. When your merit is complete and your practice fulfilled, faith and aspiration supporting one another
faith and aspiration mutually relying on and reinforcing the power of mindfulness
, at the moment of death you will surely be born in the highest grade.
Venerable Huxi

For the matter of true faith and practice, you must genuinely seek to be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss in the West, and with a single, concentrated thought hold to the one phrase of Amitabha Buddha
This one thought alone is our original teacher
this one thought alone is the manifested Buddha
this one thought alone is the fierce general who breaks open hell
this one thought alone is the precious sword that cuts down the host of demons
this one thought alone is the bright lamp that parts the darkness
this one thought alone is the great ship that crosses the sea of suffering
this one thought alone is the fine prescription that frees us from birth and death
this one thought alone is the shortcut out of the three realms
a shortcut
this one thought alone is Amitabha of our own nature
this one thought alone reaches the Pure Land of Mind-Only
But you need only remember
this
that the one phrase of Amitabha Buddha is being recited, and never let it drop
Let every thought be ever present before you, every thought never departing from the mind

When there is nothing to do, recite it thus; when there is something to do, recite it thus; in comfort, recite it thus; in sickness and pain, recite it thus; in life, recite it thus; in death, recite it thus
If this one thought is thus clear and undimmed, why need you ask others how to find the way home
why need you ask others how to be free of birth and death
Master Lianchi
Scattered thoughts are the illness; Buddha-recitation is the medicine
A long illness cannot be cured by a single dose, and accumulated delusion cannot be removed by a moment's recitation — the principle is the same
Pay no heed to the scattered thoughts flying about; what matters is that the recitation be earnest and keen
With every word distinct and every phrase continuing without break, hold to it with all your strength, and only then is there a share of progress toward the goal
only then is there a share of progress toward the Land of Ultimate Bliss
It is said that when true accumulation has long persisted, one day it will suddenly break open
(one day suddenly breaking open, the recitation falls away and one realizes the state of no-thought and no non-thought
— seeing the nature and awakening to the mind
This is like grinding a pestle down to a needle, or refining iron into
steel
— surely it is no empty claim
There are many gates to the Way, but this one gate is the shortest path; do not neglect it
Do not neglect it

blocks.text: Never Apart from the One Thought

inline.s: This path
the Dharma gate of Buddha-recitation
is most profound and most wonderful, and at the same time most simple and most easy
Because it is simple and easy, the clever overlook it
Now birth and death are never apart from one thought, and indeed all dharmas, mundane and supramundane
are never apart from one thought
If you now use this very thought to recite the Buddha's name, how direct, how keen, how real it is
If you
pierce through to see
where this thought arises, that is Amitabha of your own nature, that is the meaning of the Patriarch's coming from the West
that is,
the First Patriarch of Chan, Bodhidharma, came from the West to this land to transmit the Dharma,
and this is
its essential purport)
Even if you do not awaken
even if you cannot see your nature and awaken to the mind

, riding on the power of this thought, you will be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, cutting straight across birth and death and escaping the cycle of rebirth, and in the end you will surely attain great awakening
I only hope you will let go of the myriad entanglements and, through the twelve watches of the day
keep each thought alert and mindful — this is my deepest wish
